findings.problem: The two `have` declarations are `rfl` equations that only restate the definitional reduction of composing a tuple with the constant map `fun _ : Fin 1 => i`. They are used solely to rewrite the type of `h.comp` for `simpa`. Since `BFEquiv.comp` returns `BFEquiv ... (a ∘ g) (b ∘ g)` and `a ∘ (fun _ => i)` is definitionally `fun _ => a i`, the coordinate tuple expected by `bfEquiv_two_rigidSixGraph_iff` is already the same type; the auxiliary equations and the `simpa` are redundant bookkeeping.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the quoted block with:

```lean
    funext i
    exact (bfEquiv_two_rigidSixGraph_iff (a i) (b i)).mp
      (h.comp (fun _ : Fin 1 => i))
```

The result of `h.comp (fun _ : Fin 1 => i)` has type `BFEquiv ... 1 (a ∘ fun _ => i) (b ∘ fun _ => i)`, which is definitionally the required `BFEquiv ... 1 (fun _ => a i) (fun _ => b i)`.
findings.benefit: Removes two auxiliary declarations that carry no mathematical content and makes the reindexing to the `i`-th coordinate explicit at the point where `BFEquiv.comp` is applied. The proof becomes shorter while the key argument—reindex the tuple to coordinate `i`, then use that level two separates single vertices—remains at least as easy to read.
